_doc: Field-wide milestones for the timeline (course-specific events live in each course.json). year < 0 means BC.

milestones.title: A mathematical model of speculation
milestones.detail: Bachelier’s dissertation modelled bond prices as a random walk and priced an option. It is the usual start of the mathematical theory of speculative prices.

milestones.title: Portfolio selection
milestones.detail: Markowitz defined risk as variance and made diversification a statement about covariance.

milestones.title: A single-factor model of expected return
milestones.detail: Sharpe’s capital asset pricing model supplied the beta that a later market-neutral constraint sets to zero.

milestones.title: The reward-to-variability ratio
milestones.detail: Sharpe defined the ratio of average excess return to the standard deviation of return, now called the Sharpe ratio.

milestones.title: Efficient capital markets
milestones.detail: Fama’s review organised the claim that prices reflect information, and the weak, semi-strong and strong forms later empirical work argues with.

milestones.title: Currency futures
milestones.detail: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange listed currency futures on 16 May 1972, giving exchange-traded prices to foreign exchange.

milestones.title: A manual of trading indicators
milestones.detail: Wilder’s New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems defined the relative strength index and treated trend and extreme readings as separate tools. The usual 14-period window is his suggestion, not a theorem.

milestones.title: Exchange rates and a random-walk benchmark
milestones.detail: Meese and Rogoff showed that standard macroeconomic models of the exchange rate did not beat a random walk out of sample.

milestones.title: The spread as adverse selection
milestones.detail: Glosten and Milgrom modelled the bid–ask spread as compensation for trading against a better-informed counterparty. A passive fill is not a free improvement on a market order.

milestones.title: Variance ratios against the random walk
milestones.detail: Lo and MacKinlay rejected the random-walk hypothesis for weekly US stock returns. Detectable dependence can still be economically small.

milestones.title: Short-horizon reversal
milestones.detail: Jegadeesh, and separately Lehmann, documented negative autocorrelation in individual US stock returns at horizons of a week to a month.

milestones.title: A computer test of simple rules
milestones.detail: Brock, Lakonishok and LeBaron tested moving-average and channel rules on the Dow Jones index. The arguments that followed — costs, data mining, out of sample — shaped modern backtesting.

milestones.title: Buying winners and selling losers
milestones.detail: Jegadeesh and Titman documented intermediate-horizon cross-sectional momentum in US stocks.

milestones.title: A traded equity basket
milestones.detail: The SPDR S&P 500 ETF began trading on 22 January 1993. An ETF backtest studies that instrument, not a hand-built stock universe.

milestones.title: A reality check for data snooping
milestones.detail: White gave a bootstrap test of whether the best rule in a large search beats a benchmark, once the search itself is counted.

milestones.title: Optimal execution
milestones.detail: Almgren and Chriss posed execution as a trade-off between market impact and the risk of waiting.

milestones.title: Sampling error of the Sharpe ratio
milestones.detail: Lo derived the distribution of the Sharpe ratio under serial correlation and showed how wide the interval is for a few years of data.

milestones.title: A specified pairs rule
milestones.detail: Gatev, Goetzmann and Rouwenhorst published a distance-based pairs strategy whose matching, entry, exit and delay are explicit enough to argue with.

milestones.title: Time series momentum
milestones.detail: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen documented a positive relation between an asset’s own past return and its next return across futures markets. It is an average historical relation, not a rule for one ETF.

milestones.title: Backtest overfitting named
milestones.detail: Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado and Zhu showed how easily a search produces an attractive in-sample equity curve, and Bailey and López de Prado published the deflated Sharpe ratio as a correction for selection.

milestones.title: Momentum crashes
milestones.detail: Daniel and Moskowitz showed that momentum portfolios have episodic left-tail losses, concentrated in volatile rebounds after declines.

milestones.title: The factor zoo and multiple testing
milestones.detail: Harvey, Liu and Zhu argued that published t-statistics in the cross-section of expected returns overstate the evidence, because so many factors have been tried.

milestones.title: Purged validation for financial labels
milestones.detail: López de Prado’s Advances in Financial Machine Learning set out purging and embargoes for labels that overlap in time, and made reproducibility a minimum standard.
